title: Staged Variant Router & Safety Lattice for Traffic Policies
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a composable configuration and policy engine that drives staged variant routing for model rollouts. This ticket covers: expressive traffic split grammars, step-schedule primitives (time-based and metric-based), safety lattice guardrails (latency/error/quality thresholds), and automatic rollback hooks. The goal is a developer-facing, declarative spec that operators can attach to a deployment to run canaries, A/B experiments, shadow traffic checks, and automated rollback when regressions are detected. Emphasis: observable decisions, deterministic fallback behavior, and minimal disruption to existing routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: A1: API for declarative rollout policies exists and validates against schema -- traffic splits, steps, metrics, and rollback rules.
A2: Runtime can execute time-based and metric-driven step transitions for a sample model deployment without manual intervention.
A3: Safety lattice enforces multi-dimensional guardrails (p90 latency, error-rate, quality-regression) and triggers auto-rollback on breach.
A4: Rollouts emit structured events to the Console (per-step traffic, reason for step transition, rollback reason) and are queryable in the rollout dashboard.
A5: Integration tests cover: gradual ramp-up, A/B split evaluation, shadow-only traffic paths, and rollback on synthetic metric spikes.
A6: Backwards compatibility: policies with only time/traffic fields continue to behave as before; invalid fields fail fast with descriptive errors.
A7: Security review sign-off recorded and policy evaluation runs in the customer tenant boundary for Private deployments.
A8: Documentation and example policy templates are published in the model-lifecycle Confluence space.
A9: Performance regression: policy evaluation adds <3ms median overhead per decision in the routing hot path (measured under 10k RPS test harness).
implementation_steps: Design: define a compact, composable schema for rollout policies (traffic, steps, metrics, thresholds, cooldowns, fallbacks). Draft in Confluence and review with PM/Design (1.5d).
Schema: implement JSON Schema + server-side validation (1d).
Engine: add a policy evaluation module in the routing service that can: parse policies, keep step state, evaluate metrics, and decide transitions (4d).
Metrics: instrument rollout-specific metrics and events (per-step traffic_pct, decision_reason, guardrail_violations) and export to telemetry layer (1d).
Console: add a minimal rollout timeline panel that subscribes to rollout events and displays current step, traffic splits, and recent violations (2d).
E2E Tests: create deterministic harness for time-based and metric-based transitions including chaos scenarios (2d).
Performance: run 10k RPS benchmarks to tune policy evaluation hot path and add caching for static policies (1d).
Documentation: publish policy examples (canary, A/B, shadow) and migration notes (1d).
Security Review: submit for security review and address concerns around policy eval in Private deployments (1d).
Rollout: ship behind feature flag, enable for internal tenants, collect telemetry, then enable for broader customers after 1 week of monitoring (2d).
config_examples:
# Time-based canary
name: quick-canary
traffic:
  - variant: v1
    pct: 100
  - variant: v2
    pct: 0
steps:
  - at: 2026-03-10T15:00:00Z
    set_traffic:
      v2: 5
  - after: 30m
    set_traffic:
      v2: 25
  - after: 1h
    set_traffic:
      v2: 50
rollback: 
  on_thresholds:
    latency_p90_ms: 1200
    error_rate_pct: 1.5

# Metric-driven progressive rollout
name: metric-progressive
traffic: {v1:85, v2:15}
steps:
  - hold: 15m
    until:
      - metric: user_stated_quality_delta
        comparator: '<='
        value: 0.02
  - increase: 20
    cooldown: 10m
rollback:
  auto: true
  require_confirmation: false
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Policy eval could be a hot-path overhead. Mitigation: lightweight evaluator inlined with caching and fast-path for static policies; ensure <3ms median overhead (see perf step).

Risk: False positives on rollback due to noisy metrics. Mitigation: require sustained violation windows and use composite signals (latency + error + quality) before auto-rollback; allow operator override and cooldowns.
Risk: Complex policies are hard for customers to author. Mitigation: provide templates (canary, A/B, shadow) and a validator with actionable errors and UI wizard in Console.

Risk: Security surface for Private deployments if policy eval leaks telemetry. Mitigation: ensure policy evaluation and logs remain in tenant boundary and honor KMS/Audit settings; include in security review.
Risk: Inconsistent behavior across Dedicated/Hosted/Private. Mitigation: enforce the same schema and run policy unit tests across deployment modes during release gating.
